title: User guide
intro: Step-by-step guide to using {{product}} (VulnScanner engine). Button labels match the UI. This page has no production hosts, IPs, or credentials — replace example targets with assets you are authorized to test.
mulai1: Open the app login page. No account yet? register via <ui>Register</ui> (email + password).
mulai2: Verify email if asked (inbox link / <ui>Verify email</ui> flow). Unverified accounts usually cannot scan.
mulai3: Log in. Confirm the header shows credit balance and the sidebar shows navigation (Dashboard, scanners, Schedules, Guard, Host Protect, etc.).
mulai4: If you have more than one organization, pick the active workspace in the org switcher (top / sidebar). All scans and schedules bind to the <ui>active org</ui>.
mulai5: Open <dash>Dashboard</dash> for history overview and shortcuts.
ip2: Check the credit preview on the form (IP scan cost). Low balance → top up first (see Credits).
ip3: Fill Target IP address (an IPv4 you control). Optional: adjust Port range (default 1-1000, or e.g. 22,80,443).
ip4: Click Start IP scan. Wait for Initializing scan… then you are redirected to Scan details (/scan/:id).
ip5: Watch the status badge (<ui>pending</ui> / <ui>running</ui> → <ui>completed</ui> or <ui>failed</ui>). Progress may also show on the <ui>Scan progress</ui> card if you stay on the scanner page.
ipNote: Typical coverage: ports/services (nmap), OSV CVEs, severity, OS fingerprint when available.
dom2: Fill <ui>Target domain</ui> (a hostname you own). Optional: <ui>Try example.com</ui> is only for trying the UI flow — do not treat public lab results as a production audit.
dom3: Check credit cost, then click <ui>Start domain scan</ui>.
dom4: Follow the redirect to scan detail; wait for <ui>completed</ui>.
domNote: Typical coverage: DNS/subdomains, TLS, security headers, tech fingerprint.
mob2: Pick platform (Android / iOS). Android: .apk / .aab. iOS: .ipa. Max file size follows the UI (hundreds of MB).
mob3: Drag-and-drop or choose a file. Extension must match the platform.
mob4: Check credits (apk / ipa are billed separately), then start upload/scan from the form.
mob5: After the job is created, open <ui>Scan details</ui> and wait until it finishes.
mobNote: Typical coverage: manifest/permissions, exported components, hardcoded secrets, platform binary checks.
res1: On <ui>Scan details</ui>, read the severity summary, <ui>Findings</ui> table, and <ui>Scan info</ui> card (time, target, type).
res2: If the scan came from a recurring schedule, watch the baseline diff strip (new / resolved findings) when available.
res3: Download reports from the top-right buttons:
res4: Need another scan of a similar target: click <ui>Re-scan</ui> (back to the matching scanner form).
res5: History is also on the Dashboard; open a scan row for the same detail.
jadIntro: The <ui>viewer</ui> role is read-only — cannot create/edit schedules. Org admin/member/owner: continue.
jad2: See <ui>Kuota jadwal aktif</ui> (e.g. N/10). Full → disable an old schedule first.
jad4: Click <ui>Buat jadwal</ui>. The schedule appears under <ui>Jadwal Anda</ui>.
jad5: Per row: <ui>Aktifkan</ui> / <ui>Nonaktifkan</ui>, download <ui>Eksekutif</ui> from the last scan, open <ui>scan terakhir</ui> / <ui>buka scan</ui> in run history, delete if needed.
jad6: Each run deducts personal credits. Empty balance → the schedule may disable with a credits error.
aIntro: Named IP/domain targets for this workspace, with a SKU hard cap (Basic 1 / Pro 3 / Multi 10). Use assets so schedules and pack export have a stable name — not a full CMDB.
a1: Sidebar → <as>Assets</as>. Title: <ui>Assets</ui>. Check the SKU quota line (count / limit).
a2: Click <ui>Add asset</ui> (or <ui>Add your first asset</ui> when empty). Fill <ui>Name</ui>, <ui>Target</ui>, <ui>Type</ui> (IP or domain), optional <ui>Notes</ui>, then <ui>Save</ui>.
a3: Per row: <ui>Create schedule</ui> (weekly by default) if the asset has no schedule yet; <ui>Delete</ui> if you no longer need it. Cap full → remove an old asset first.
a4: Optional: <ui>Download pack JSON</ui> for an org-scoped export of named targets. Do not put production IPs into public tickets.
ws2: <ui>Buat organisasi</ui>: fill <ui>Nama</ui>, optional <ui>Slug</ui>, click <ui>Buat workspace</ui>. You become owner.
ws3: Switch the active org so scans/schedules land in the right workspace.
ws4: Owner/admin: invite members — email + role (member / viewer / admin as in the UI), send invite. Status is in the invite list; can be revoked.
ws5: Invitee: open the invite link (URL with token) → <ui>Terima undangan</ui> card → click <ui>Terima undangan</ui> while logged in.
ws6: See the Anggota list and roles. Platform admin (is_admin) is not the same as org admin — global /admin panel.
cr1: See balance in the header (Credits chip).
cr2: Before a scan, the form shows a cost preview. Start is disabled if not eligible.
cr3: After a scan, check <ch>Credit History</ch> for deductions / refunds (failed scans often auto-refund).
cr4: Top-up in v1: via invoice / provider admin — not an in-app card form. Contact AM/ops if the balance is empty.
cr5: Remember: credits are <ui>personal</ui> (not a shared org wallet).
gIntro: Per-org agent inventory + critical alerts. Not full SIEM / raw logs. Only org admin/owner can enable and create tokens. Host setup below is generic (placeholders) — no lab/prod addresses in the public doc.
g2: <ui>Status</ui> card: confirm the active org. If <ui>nonaktif</ui>, admin clicks <ui>Aktifkan Guard</ui>. Module status: <ui>nyala</ui> or <ui>nonaktif</ui>.
g3: Once on, admin: <ui>Token enroll</ui> card → optional label → <ui>Buat token</ui>. Copy the raw token immediately (shown once). The UI shows <ui>Langkah host (setelah token)</ui> plus a curl example — use that on the host. Do not paste tokens into public chat/repos.
gHostLead: On the target host (an asset you legally control), follow this order:
gCurlLead: Example enroll from the host (replace app origin & token; no JWT):
gEndpoint: Public org-bound endpoint via token: POST /api/guard/enroll body { token, agent_name }. Response: agent_id, agent_key, manager_host, install_hint.
gInstallLead: Agent runtime install on the target host (per distro, no lab secrets):
gHostCmds: Commands on the target host (by distro)
g7: Click <ui>Sinkronkan</ui> (admin) to refresh the projection. See the <ui>Agen</ui> table (online / disconnected / pending) and <ui>Alert kritis</ui>.
g8: Viewer+: can only view agents/alerts after Guard is enabled — no token generation.
g9: Quick troubleshooting: enroll 4xx → token expired/revoked/wrong org; agent pending too long → check host connectivity to manager_host from the response + Sync; do not use Manager passwords on the host.
sIntro: Separate module from Guard. Controlled event search (not Wazuh Discover / dashboards) and cases in-app. Flag SIEM_ENABLED must be on in the environment; if off, the page shows the module is inactive.
s1: Install agents in <g>Guard</g> first. Without org agents, SIEM shows empty copy.
s2: Open Sidebar → <siem>SIEM</siem>. Time filter (WIB), min level, agent, search box, then <ui>Terapkan</ui>.
s3: Click a result row for projected detail (not raw logs). Member+ can <ui>Buat kasus</ui> from an event.
s4: Owner/admin change case status <ui>terbuka</ui> / <ui>diakui</ui> / <ui>ditutup</ui>. Member+ add notes (no raw log dumps).
uIntro: Outside-in HTTP and TCP checks for this workspace (SKU seat cap). Separate from Guard/SIEM and from scan schedules. Flag UPTIME_ENABLED is on by default; if off, the page shows the module is inactive.
u1: Sidebar → <up>Uptime</up>. Title: <ui>Uptime</ui>. Read the SKU line (enabled count / limit).
u2: Click <ui>Add monitor</ui> (or <ui>Add your first monitor</ui>). Fill <ui>Name</ui>, <ui>Target</ui> (URL or host:port), <ui>Type</ui> HTTP or TCP, <ui>Interval (seconds)</ui>, optional <ui>Keyword</ui> and <ui>Notify email</ui>, then <ui>Save</ui>.
u3: Watch state badges <ui>up</ui> / <ui>down</ui> / <ui>unknown</ui>. Per row: <ui>Pause</ui> / <ui>Resume</ui>, <ui>Delete</ui>. Seat full → pause or delete an old monitor.
u4: Email down/up is best-effort (SMTP must be configured by ops). Never put raw monitor IPs on a public status page — that mapping is display-name only.
spIntro: One published public page per org, driven by Uptime monitors. Incidents are posted by hand. Publish requires org SKU pro or multi. Custom hostname is multi only. TLS for customer hosts is Cloudflare for SaaS — not ACME in the app.
sp1: Create at least one Uptime monitor first (previous section).
sp2: Sidebar → <sp>Status page</sp>. If empty, fill <ui>Slug</ui> + <ui>Title</ui> and click <ui>Create page</ui>.
sp3: Add component: pick a Monitor, set a public Display name (never the raw URL/IP), save. Then Publish. Public URL is /status/{slug} on the platform host.
sp4: Post <ui>New incident</ui> with impact/status + <ui>Update</ui> text when you need customer-facing comms. <ui>Unpublish</ui> hides the public page.
sp5: Custom hostname (Multi SKU): set <ui>Custom hostname</ui>, point a CNAME at the documented target, then <ui>Verify DNS</ui>. Do not expect in-app certificates.
hpIntro: On-box web malware for a Guard-enrolled VPS. Scan jobs run on the host via the Host Protect helper (timer + token), not on the SaaS worker. Not Imunify, not Guard alerts, not SIEM search. Quarantine isolates a file; it does not reconstruct the site.
hp1: Enroll a Guard agent first (see Guard) — wazuh-agent is not installed by the helper. On Guard, copy the agent UUID and (admin) generate a Host Protect helper token — shown once; not the enroll token. Then on that VPS, copy packaging/host-protect-helper/sinexis-install.sh from a checkout or GitHub Release (verify SHA256; do not curl | bash). Run sudo ./sinexis-install.sh --agent-id <Guard UUID> --token-file /path --api-base https://sinexis.app or --interactive on a TTY. The wrapper writes /etc/sinexis/host-protect.env (mode 600: SINEXIS_HOST_AGENT_TOKEN, SINEXIS_AGENT_ID) and enables sinexis-host-protect@.timer (poll every 5 minutes). Missing env → helper exit 4. Optional: dpkg -i sinexis-host-protect_*.deb then the same wrapper with --deb. Sidebar → Host Protect. If the page says the module is off, ops has not enabled Host Protect on this environment.
hp2: Click <ui>Add site</ui> only after the helper has polled (last helper poll on the agent). Fill <ui>Name</ui>, <ui>Root path</ui> on the agent, <ui>Guard agent</ui>, optional CMS hint. Guard enroll alone is not enough — Scan now fails closed until the helper polls. Hits are not mixed with IP/domain findings.
hp3: Critical classes (webshell / backdoor) email the site owner once per new path+rule. Re-scans update last-seen only — no second mail. File contents are never attached.
hp4: <ui>Quarantine</ui> / <ui>Restore</ui> / <ui>Ignore</ui> are isolate actions. Reconstruct (CMS restore, backup) is a hybrid ticket — not an in-app rewrite.
hp5: Open the WAF tab. Default per-site mode is off. detect logs on the customer nginx snippet. protect is Host Multi only: it sets SecRuleEngine On (403 deny) on that same customer VPS. Use Copy nginx snippet on the customer VPS only — never paste it onto the Sinexis public edge. Simulate request is a control-plane lab, not live traffic. Optional Hourly malware scans still cap two in-flight jobs per org.
t1: Only scan / enroll assets you legally control.
t2: Do not store passwords, API keys, or internal addresses in public tickets / casual screenshots.
t3: Guard v1 = inventory + critical alerts + enroll — not SOAR or a customer manager dashboard. Uptime is outside-in probes, not an SLA. Status page never exposes monitor URL/IP. Host Protect quarantine ≠ reconstruct. Host WAF is a control plane + snippet, not Coraza on sinexis.app.
